info.title: py32cli
info.description: Cross-platform, scriptable CLI for programming and inspecting Puya PY32/MS32 Cortex-M0 microcontrollers.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: py32cli - cross-platform CLI for programming Puya PY32 microcontrollers.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

commands.name: devices
commands.description: Inspect the bundled Puya PY32/MS32 device catalog.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List known part numbers in the bundled catalog.

options.name: --filter
options.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the part number, e.g. PY32F002.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show the full memory layout for one part number.

commands.name: ports
commands.description: Serial port discovery.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List serial ports visible to the OS.

commands.name: bootloader
commands.description: Talk to the PY32 ROM USART/USB ISP bootloader (system-memory boot mode).

commands.name: info
commands.description: Connect and report protocol version / product ID.

options.name: --port
options.description: Serial port, e.g. COM17 or /dev/ttyUSB0.

options.name: --baud
options.description: Baud rate. [default: 115200]

options.name: --auto-remove-rdp
options.description: If read protection is blocking access after connecting, remove it (mass-erases flash) and reconnect automatically, mirroring CubeProgrammer 1.1.0.3's 'Auto remove RDP'. Value is the catalog part number to read RAM geometry from, e.g. PY32F040xB.

options.name: --connect-timeout
options.description: Keep retrying the connection, with a spinner, for up to this many seconds (e.g. 10) instead of a single instant attempt. Useful when powering up or plugging in the target after starting the command.

commands.name: program
commands.description: Write a binary or Intel HEX file to flash.

options.name: --port
options.description: Serial port, e.g. COM17 or /dev/ttyUSB0.

options.name: --baud
options.description: Baud rate. [default: 115200]

options.name: --address
options.description: Start address, e.g. 0x08000000. Required for raw binaries; must be omitted for .hex files, whose records carry their own addresses.

options.name: --file
options.description: Binary (.bin) or Intel HEX (.hex) file to program.

options.name: --erase
options.description: Erase strategy before programming: 'mass' or 'none'.

options.name: --verify
options.description: Read back and compare after programming. [default: False]

options.name: --auto-remove-rdp
options.description: If read protection is blocking access after connecting, remove it (mass-erases flash) and reconnect automatically, mirroring CubeProgrammer 1.1.0.3's 'Auto remove RDP'. Value is the catalog part number to read RAM geometry from, e.g. PY32F040xB.

options.name: --run-to-app
options.description: After programming, jump to the lowest address written this session (the application's own reset handler) instead of leaving the chip in the bootloader. [default: False]

options.name: --connect-timeout
options.description: Keep retrying the connection, with a spinner, for up to this many seconds (e.g. 10) instead of a single instant attempt. Useful when powering up or plugging in the target after starting the command.

options.name: --baud

options.name: --address
options.description: Address to jump to, e.g. 0x08000000.

options.name: --connect-timeout

commands.name: option-bytes
commands.description: Read and write a device's option-bytes bank over the UART bootloader.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Read and decode the option-bytes bank from real hardware.

options.name: --port
options.description: Serial port, e.g. COM17 or /dev/ttyUSB0.

options.name: --baud
options.description: Baud rate. [default: 115200]

options.name: --device
options.description: Catalog part number to decode against, e.g. PY32F040xB. The bootloader has no chip auto-detection, so this must be supplied explicitly.

options.name: --connect-timeout
options.description: Keep retrying the connection, with a spinner, for up to this many seconds (e.g. 10) instead of a single instant attempt. Useful when powering up or plugging in the target after starting the command.

commands.name: write
commands.description: Change option-byte fields and write them to the chip. DESTRUCTIVE: a wrong RDP, write-protect, or boot-mode value can make the chip unreachable over this same interface. Without --confirm, this only prints what would change.

options.name: --port
options.description: Serial port, e.g. COM17 or /dev/ttyUSB0.

options.name: --baud
options.description: Baud rate. [default: 115200]

options.name: --device
options.description: Catalog part number to decode against, e.g. PY32F040xB. The bootloader has no chip auto-detection, so this must be supplied explicitly.

options.name: --set
options.description: Comma-separated FIELD=VALUE pairs, e.g. NRST_MODE=1,nBOOT1=0. Values are the field's raw numeric option value (hex 0x.. or decimal) — the same value shown in 'option-bytes show', not its display text.

options.name: --from-current
options.description: Read the option-bytes bank from hardware first and edit that, instead of starting from factory defaults. Recommended for real use. [default: False]

options.name: --confirm
options.description: Actually write to the chip. Without this, only prints the planned final state and exits without touching hardware. [default: False]

options.name: --connect-timeout
options.description: Keep retrying the connection, with a spinner, for up to this many seconds (e.g. 10) instead of a single instant attempt. Useful when powering up or plugging in the target after starting the command.

commands.name: read
commands.description: Read target memory over SWD (no flash algorithm needed for reads).

options.name: --address
options.description: Start address, e.g. 0x08000000.

options.name: --length
options.description: Number of bytes to read. Accepts decimal (256), hex (0x100), or a binary unit suffix (64kB, 1MB).

options.name: --out
options.description: File to write the dump to.

options.name: --reboot-target
options.description: Power-cycle the target's VCC while connecting (matches the official GUI's own connect default). Adds a real delay (~11s) to this command. Needed after clearing RDP over PY-Link — a plain option-bytes rewrite and even a physical NRST press were not enough on real hardware to restore flash access; only a genuine power cycle re-evaluated the read-protection gate. [default: False]

options.name: --speed
options.description: SWD clock speed: very-high (8 MHz), high (5 MHz), standard (1 MHz, default), low (500 kHz). [default: standard]

options.name: --connect-timeout
options.description: Keep retrying the connection, with a spinner, for up to this many seconds (e.g. 10) instead of a single instant attempt. Useful when powering up or plugging in the target after starting the command.

commands.name: reset
commands.description: Reset the target so it runs from its own reset vector. As a standalone command this has NOT been confirmed to actually resume execution on hardware where a prior session left the core halted (a physical reset was needed in that case) — 'program --run-to-app' calling the same Reset within the session that just loaded the flash algorithm DID work. See plan.md Phase 4.

options.name: --speed
options.description: SWD clock speed: very-high (8 MHz), high (5 MHz), standard (1 MHz, default), low (500 kHz). [default: standard]

options.name: --connect-timeout
options.description: Keep retrying the connection, with a spinner, for up to this many seconds (e.g. 10) instead of a single instant attempt. Useful when powering up or plugging in the target after starting the command.

commands.name: erase
commands.description: Erase every sector the device's MAIN_FLASH algorithm describes. There is no separate chip-erase in this vendor protocol — the reference tool always erases sector-by-sector, see plan.md Phase 4 — so this is the only erase mode.

options.name: --device
options.description: Catalog part number to read RAM geometry and the flash algorithm from, e.g. PY32F040xB. PY-Link has no chip auto-detection, so this must be supplied explicitly.

options.name: --speed
options.description: SWD clock speed: very-high (8 MHz), high (5 MHz), standard (1 MHz, default), low (500 kHz). [default: standard]

options.name: --connect-timeout
options.description: Keep retrying the connection, with a spinner, for up to this many seconds (e.g. 10) instead of a single instant attempt. Useful when powering up or plugging in the target after starting the command.

commands.name: program
commands.description: Write a binary or Intel HEX file to flash via SWD (uploads the device's flash algorithm first).

options.name: --device
options.description: Catalog part number to read RAM geometry and the flash algorithm from, e.g. PY32F040xB. PY-Link has no chip auto-detection, so this must be supplied explicitly.

options.name: --address
options.description: Start address, e.g. 0x08000000. Required for raw binaries; must be omitted for .hex files, whose records carry their own addresses.

options.name: --file
options.description: Binary (.bin) or Intel HEX (.hex) file to program.

options.name: --erase
options.description: Erase strategy before programming: 'mass' (erase every sector) or 'none'.

options.name: --verify
options.description: Read back and compare after programming. [default: False]

options.name: --run-to-app
options.description: Reset the target after programming so it runs the freshly-written image, within the same session (not yet confirmed to actually resume execution on its own — see plan.md Phase 4). [default: False]

options.name: --speed
options.description: SWD clock speed: very-high (8 MHz), high (5 MHz), standard (1 MHz, default), low (500 kHz). [default: standard]

options.name: --skip-unchanged
options.description: Read each page back first and skip writing it if the target already holds exactly that data (e.g. re-running program with the same file). Off by default: after a mass erase almost every page differs from the erased state anyway, so this would just add a read round-trip per page for no benefit there — only worth it for a likely no-op re-run or resuming a partial write. [default: False]

options.name: --connect-timeout
options.description: Keep retrying the connection, with a spinner, for up to this many seconds (e.g. 10) instead of a single instant attempt. Useful when powering up or plugging in the target after starting the command.

commands.name: console
commands.description: Interactive memory-only REPL over PY-Link: 'peek <addr> <len>' reads and hex-dumps memory, 'poke <addr> <hex-bytes>' writes raw bytes (e.g. 'poke 0x20000000 AABBCCDD'). No registers, no breakpoints, no step — PY-Link's vendor protocol has none of those. 'poke' targeting flash is untested and not recommended; use 'pylink program'/'option-bytes write' for that.
